statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). CME equity futures completed their weekly settlement at 21:00Z on Friday, so the entire published 24-hour window covers a halted market in which no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop.
recommendation: Tail sits at a weekend floor and no danger window is published, because the forecast horizon contains no U.S. cash session and no CME futures session. The scores describe deferred gap and headline risk rather than observable intraday structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection rules are unaffected by this assessment. The first genuine repricing checkpoint is the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which falls outside this window; the first scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index on Monday.
headline: Weekend halt follows a hawkish-Warsh Friday: NQ settles at 29,509.50 with equity volatility contained
body: Friday's Jackson Hole speech by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reset September policy expectations, with market-implied odds of a rate increase rising to roughly 57-60% from about 35% beforehand. The repricing was expressed mainly in rates: the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.72%, up about 4bp, the 2-year rose about 11bp to 4.34%, and the 30-year ended near 5.21%. Equity damage stayed contained and internally split. Cash NDX closed at 29,433.43 (-0.70%) within a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range and NQ futures settled the week at 29,509.50 (-0.63%), both in the lower part of their session ranges, but the decline was rotational: semiconductors gave back much of Thursday's Nvidia-led rally while other large-cap index members held up better. VIX eased to 14.43, so implied volatility did not confirm a stress event. Energy remained a stabilising input, with WTI at $83.44 after a roughly 4% weekly decline and Brent at $88.29. The published window now covers a fully halted market: CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, which is outside this horizon, and no U.S. macro release is scheduled before Monday. Tail is therefore held at a weekend floor, since a persistent no-retracement path requires continuous trading, while Stress decays to a low-20s baseline and drifts up modestly late on Saturday as the interval of unpriced weekend information widens. Confidence stays in the high band on complete verified Friday evidence and eases only as that observation ages.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours span the quiet overnight stretch before Jackson Hole, the Warsh repricing itself and the weekly settlement. Overnight Asian and European hours held Tail near 11-13 with Stress around 50 and a mixed mode. Tail and Stress lifted through the U.S. morning as the speech reset September rate expectations, peaking at Tail 22 and Stress 64 in the 17:00Z hour with an event/whipsaw mode while yields rose and gold fell. Price discovery stayed orderly: retracements occurred, VIX eased rather than spiked and the decline was rotational rather than broad, so Tail never approached the block threshold and the mapped state stayed between EA_ON and WATCH. Scores fell back sharply into the 21:00Z settlement as the session closed without a one-way extension. One clock hour, 10:00Z, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published window runs from the current hour through Saturday 21:00Z and contains no cash session, no CME futures session and no scheduled U.S. release. With no venue open, the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot form, so Tail is held at a 6-8 floor throughout and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window. Stress decays from the mid-20s to a low-20s overnight baseline before drifting back up modestly through Saturday as the interval of unpriced weekend information widens ahead of the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, which lies outside this horizon. Confidence starts at 85 and eases to 81 purely as the last live observation ages. Weekend Jackson Hole commentary and any Middle East development are treated as discovery for the reopening gap and would be verified against primary sources before they affected scoring.
